pages.title: Start here: how this workspace runs

text.text: A ten-minute tour for every trainer and whoever does the books. Read it once, then work from the rhythm checklist.
What lives where
Packages and prices
: what you sell, sessions included, session length, where you train and how long a pack lasts.
Clients

: goal, main trainer, current package, health and injury notes (confidential), when they did the health questions and when their program is next reviewed. Sessions done, no-shows, check-ins and money add up by themselves.
Programs
: one row per training block, with the phase, days a week, main lifts and progress so far.
Packages sold
: every pack a client bought, sessions used and left, and when it expires.
Sessions
: every session, assessment, program review and video call, with what you worked on and how hard it felt.
Weekly check-ins
: what online and hybrid clients send each week, and whether you have replied.
Payments
: packs, monthly coaching, assessments and late cancel fees.
A client's path
An enquiry comes in through the form and becomes a
Lead
. Call within a day and book the assessment.
At the assessment, the client answers the health questions. Anything flagged needs a doctor's clearance before hard training. Record the baseline numbers on the client page.
They buy a package. Add the payment and a row in
Packages sold
, then write their first program as a Draft and set it to Running at the first session.
Each session is a row in
Sessions
linked to the package.
Mark done
after it; sessions left drop by one.
Online and hybrid clients send the weekly check-in form. Reply within a day.
At the review date, retest, note the progress, finish the program and write the next one.
When two sessions are left, talk about the next package.
Who does what
Trainers
: their sessions, programs, check-in replies and renewals.
Assistant coach
: session set-up, marking sessions, chasing leads.
Bookkeeper
: payments, failed cards, monthly coaching billing.
Your rhythm
Every day: mark yesterday's sessions; reply to check-ins due today
Every Monday: program reviews due this week; leads to call
Every week: packages with two or fewer sessions left; failed payments
Every month: no-show patterns; packages expiring with sessions left
Making it yours

Change the packages and prices first, then add your clients. Delete the sample clients once your own are in. Health notes and bodyweights are confidential; only the trainers who work with that client should read them.
Sessions, check-ins, renewals and money. Look at it every Monday.
Check-in replies overdue
Program reviews this week
Sessions not marked yet
Money not yet in (pending and failed)
Active packages
A renewal is earned in the sessions before the last one, by showing the client how far they have come.
When to talk about it
When a package has two sessions left, its
Renewal

column reads Talk about the next package. Bring it up in that session, not the final one. In the last session the client is already thinking about what comes after, and a surprise ask feels like a sale. Two sessions out, it feels like planning.
How to have the conversation
Open the client's program and their first session notes. Pick two numbers that have changed: a lift, a walk time, a pain score, how many push-ups.
Show them. Say what the numbers mean in their life: carrying the shopping up the stairs, keeping up on a hike, no back pain at work.
Say what the next block would aim for, in one sentence.

Offer the package that fits. A client who came weekly and kept every session suits the 20-pack. A client who travels might suit hybrid coaching. Someone who has the routine down might move to online coaching at a lower monthly cost.
If they say yes, take payment before the next session and add a row to
Packages sold
. If they want to think, set a reminder for the last session. If they say no, thank them and ask what would bring them back.
Price and terms
Packages are paid in full before the first session in them.
Packs expire: 10 sessions in 120 days, 20 in 210 days. Write the expiry date when you sell it.
No-shows and cancellations with less than 24 hours' notice use a session. Say this when you sell, and in the welcome email.
One extension of the expiry for illness or injury, decided by the owner. Write why on the package page.
Finished clients
When a client does not renew, set them to
Finished

, not deleted. Their history stays: if they come back in a year, their old program and numbers are the place to start. Send a short note at three months asking how training is going on their own. Many come back for a block before a holiday, a race or a wedding.
Each month
How many packages ended, and how many renewed.
Packages that expired with sessions left: those clients drifted. Call them.
Which trainer's clients renew most, and what they do differently.
The assessment decides whether a client trusts you. Make it about them, keep it safe, and send them away with a plan.
Before they arrive
Booking in Sessions as an Assessment, 75 minutes
Health questions sent by email to fill in ahead of time
Studio set up: scale, tape measure, a box, a light kettlebell, a band
The health questions

Every client answers the same short health questionnaire before exercising: heart conditions, chest pain, dizziness, joint or bone problems, medication, recent surgery, pregnancy. If they answer yes to anything, they need a note from their doctor before you train them hard. Write what they told you in
Health and injury notes
(only trainers who work with them see it) and fill in
Health questions done
The conversation (20 minutes)
Ask what made them reach out now. Write their answer word for word as the
Main goal
Ask what they have tried before and what got in the way.
Ask how many days a week they can really train, and where.
Ask about sleep, work and stress. They shape what a good program looks like.
The movement screen (25 minutes)
Sit to stand from a box, ten times.
Bodyweight squat, from the front and side.
Hinge with a dowel along the back.
Push-up from the floor or a bench.
Single-leg balance, each side.
A walk or a short run, if it fits their goal.
Write the results as starting numbers on the client page: they are what you show them at the renewal.
The first workout (20 minutes)
End with a short session they can do. Three moves, done well, with a little effort. Ask how it felt on a scale of one to ten and write it in
Effort
. They should leave feeling capable, not wrecked.
After
Mark the assessment done.
Within a day, send a short summary: their goal, what you saw, and what you recommend.
When they buy, add the payment and the package, and write their first program as a Draft.
Your hour is your product. A clear rule, said kindly and applied evenly, protects it without losing clients.
The rule

A session cancelled with less than 24 hours' notice, or missed, uses a session from the package. Clients on monthly coaching pay a late cancel fee instead. Say this when they buy, put it in the welcome email, and apply it the same way to everyone.
Marking it
After the session time, open
Not marked yet
on the main page.
Set a session the client missed with no word to
No-show
Set one cancelled inside 24 hours to
Late cancel
For monthly coaching clients, add a Late cancel fee payment of 35 dollars.
The client's
No-shows and late cancels
count goes up, and the package's
Sessions left
goes down.
The first time

Send a short, friendly message the same day: you missed them, you hope everything is all right, and here is the next session. Mention that the session came off the package, in one plain sentence. Most people apologise and it does not happen again.
When it keeps happening
At two misses, the
Next step

column says Talk about attendance. Have that conversation in person, at the start of the next session. Ask what is getting in the way: the time of day, work, childcare, motivation. Often the answer is a different slot, fewer sessions a week, or moving to hybrid coaching so they can train when it suits them.
When to waive it
A real emergency: illness, a family emergency, a car accident.
Your own mistake: a double booking, a wrong time in the reminder.
Once a year, at the trainer's discretion, for a client who never misses.
When you waive it, set the session to Cancelled instead, and write why in the session notes.
Reminders that work
A text the evening before with the time and place.
For in-home and park sessions, the address and a note on the weather.
For early-morning clients, a reminder two evenings before as well.
Online clients stay when they feel seen. The weekly check-in, answered well and on time, is how they feel it.
How it works
Every online and hybrid client sends the
Weekly check-in
form at the end of their week: how many workouts they did against the plan, energy, sleep, bodyweight if they track it, their best moment and their hardest one. Each one lands in
Weekly check-ins
marked To reply, with a reply-by date one day later.
Replying
Open
Replies overdue
first, then today's.
Read the check-in alongside the client's program and the last two check-ins.
Reply in three parts: one thing they did well (be specific), one thing to adjust next week, and one question.
Change the program if needed, and say so in the reply.
Set the check-in to
Replied
Keep replies to five or six sentences. A short, specific reply on time beats a long one two days late.
Reading the numbers
Done (%)
under 75 for two weeks in a row: the plan is too big for their life right now. Cut a day, or make the sessions shorter.
Energy under 5 with poor sleep: lighten the week. Progress follows recovery.
Bodyweight: look at the trend over four weeks, never a single week.
When a check-in does not arrive

If a client misses a check-in, send a short message the next day: no pressure, just checking in. Two missed check-ins in a row needs a call. Clients who go quiet are often about to cancel; a call while they are still a client is easier than winning them back.
Each month

Book the monthly video call that comes with the plan. Look at the four check-ins together, set the goal for the next month, and update the program. Note the call as a session with the kind set to Video call.
